title: TUM, NEURA Robotics Launch World's Largest AI Robotics Training Center
summary: TUM's Institute of Robotics and Machine Intelligence (MIRMI) and NEURA Robotics signed a cooperation agreement on August 11, 2026 to build 'TUM RoboGym (powered by NEURA),' described as the world's largest robotics research and training center, inside the TUM Convergence Centre in Munich. The partners are jointly investing roughly €17 million, with NEURA contributing about €11 million largely toward robot hardware and maintenance. The hub, led by MIRMI professors Lorenzo Masia and Achim Lilienthal, will train hundreds of robot systems, many humanoid, from human demonstrations, feeding data into NEURA's Neuraverse platform. NEURA closed a $1.4 billion Series C in June 2026, which underwrites its side of the investment.
whyItMatters: Pairing a major European university robotics institute with a well-funded humanoid vendor to build large-scale physical training infrastructure is a concrete bet that training-data and facility scale, not just algorithms, are the bottleneck for humanoid deployment, and marks a notable European counterweight to U.S. and Chinese robot-training buildouts.
